No, no, not at all. That's the thing, I haven't been trying to diet or anything like that. I actually used to really enjoy eating. My wife and I, we used to go out to this little Italian place down the street on Fridays, and I'd always get the chicken parm, clean my plate, maybe even have some tiramisu after. But now? I'll be sitting on the couch, maybe watching TV or just staring out the window, and hours will go by, and it won't even occur to me that I should probably have a snack or something. It's really strange, because like I said, I'm a guy who usually appreciates a good meal, especially when my wife cooks. She made her famous pot roast the other night, the one with the carrots and potatoes that slow-cooks all day, and the whole house smelled amazing, but I just... I couldn't do it. I took maybe three bites and felt completely full, almost nauseous even. So no, definitely not trying to lose weight on purpose. It's just happening because I can't bring myself to eat.

Well... I don't really think so. I mean, the guitar was really my main thing, you know? It’s the one hobby I did every single day without fail. Back when I was taking some college classes a few years ago, I even played in this little acoustic duo at a coffee shop near campus, so it’s just always been this huge part of my identity. But as for other stuff... honestly, I haven't really noticed anything else dropping off like that. Like, I still watch TV with my wife in the evenings. And I still like sitting out on the porch in the mornings, even if I’m not eating breakfast, just watching the neighborhood wake up and the cars drive by. I used to read a bit, mostly these old, pulpy sci-fi paperbacks from the 70s with the crazy cover art, and I guess I haven't picked one of those up in a minute, but that’s really just because I haven't found a good author lately, not because of this heavy feeling. 

So, yeah, I think it really is just the guitar that stands out. It’s just so glaring because it used to be my morning ritual, my way to clear my head before the day started, and now it’s just sitting there gathering dust. But I can't really think of any other specific hobbies or anything that I've completely stopped caring about.

Well, like I was saying, it's hard to put an exact number on it since I haven't been using the scale. Five percent... I mean, I guess if I'm normally around, say, 180 pounds, five percent would be... what, like nine pounds? Honestly, yeah, I think it could easily be that much, maybe even more.

Man, that's... that's a really tough question to think about, to be honest. Because I've been trying to find something, anything, that gives me a little spark, and... I just draw a complete blank. 

Like I was mentioning earlier about the guitar—I have this really beautiful acoustic, a Martin, that my dad gave me back when I was taking some college classes in my early twenties. I used to pick it up practically every single day. I'd sit on the edge of the bed and just strum for hours, trying to learn new fingerpicking patterns or just playing old folk songs, and I'd totally lose track of time because I was just so into it. But I just sat there holding it for about five minutes, feeling absolutely nothing, and then I put it back. 

And it's not just the guitar, either. It's really everything. Even dumb, easy stuff, like video games. I used to love firing up the PlayStation and just losing myself in a big open-world game for a whole afternoon, getting really invested in the story and the characters. My wife would even sit and watch me play sometimes because the graphics are so good now, they're practically like movies. But lately, I'll turn the console on, look at the menu screen with all my games lined up, and the thought of actually starting one just feels exhausting. It's like, what's the point? 

Even watching TV or movies with my wife... we used to have these great movie nights every Friday, where we'd make a big bowl of popcorn, get all cozy on the couch under a blanket, and really get into whatever we were watching. Now I just sit there staring at the screen and I'm not even following the plot. The colors just flash by, people are talking, but I'm not absorbing any of it. It's like the color and the flavor have just been completely drained out of every single thing I used to like doing. So, no, if I'm being completely honest, I really can't think of a single activity right now that actually brings me any enjoyment. It's all just totally flat.

Without any breaks... yeah, that is exactly it. The unbroken part is what really gets to you. If we are talking about this current stretch, this specific low where it has just been a solid, heavy wall of nothing with zero relief... that has been going on for right about three weeks now.

Well, the guitar thing... it's really tied into this whole mood I've been in lately. It's been happening for about the same amount of time, these last three weeks since my wife went full-time. 

You see, playing guitar used to be my thing. I've got this beautiful acoustic, a Taylor, that I saved up for years to buy back when I was still taking some classes. And usually, I'd pick it up every day. It was my way to unwind, or to just kind of express whatever I was feeling. But lately... most days lately, I wake up with this heavy, flat feeling. It's hard to describe. It's just like... a weight on my chest, and the whole apartment just feels too quiet, too empty. And I'll look at the guitar sitting there on its stand in the corner of the living room, right where I always leave it, and I'll think, "Maybe I should play a little. Maybe that will help." And sometimes I'll even go over and pick it up. I'll sit down on the couch, rest it on my knee, put my fingers on the fretboard... and then just nothing. 

It doesn't lift me up at all anymore. There's no spark, no joy in it. I'll strum a G chord and it just sounds like noise. It feels like a chore, honestly. The physical act of pressing down the strings just feels exhausting, and the music doesn't make me feel anything. It's just flat, like everything else right now. So I end up just putting it back on the stand after a minute or two and going back to just sitting there in the quiet. It's really frustrating because I want to enjoy it, I really do, but that heavy feeling just swallows it all up. So, yeah, it's been about three weeks of just... not being able to find any comfort in it at all.
